in_cluster,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold,\n                     const int point_count) {\n    int closest_point = -1;\n    double min_diameter = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();\n    \n    // Try each unclustered point as a candidate\n    for (int candidate = 0; candidate < point_count; ++candidate) {\n        // Skip if already clustered or already in this cluster\n        if (clustered[candidate] || in_cluster[candidate]) continue;\n        \n        // Calculate the maximum distance from candidate to all cluster members\n        double max_dist = 0.0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = cluster_members[i];\n            const double dist = distance(points[candidate], points[member]);\n            max_dist = std::max(max_dist, dist);\n        }\n        \n        // If adding this point keeps diameter below threshold and is better than current best\n        if (max_dist < threshold && max_dist < min_diameter) {\n            min_diameter = max_dist;\n            closest_point = candidate;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return std::vector<bool> clustered(N, false);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered_indices;\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n    \n    // Initialize unclustered indices\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        unclustered_indices.push_back(i);\n    }\n    \n    // Main clustering loop\n    while (!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n        std::vector<int> best_cluster_members;\n        \n        // Try each unclustered point as a seed\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < unclustered_indices.size(); ++i) {\n            const int seed = clustered, points, \n                                                       threshold, N, \n                                                       &candidate_members);\n            \n            if (cardinality > max_cardinality) {\n                max_cardinality = cardinality;\n                best_seed = seed;\n                best_cluster_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found a cluster, add it\n        if (best_seed >= 0 && max_cardinality > 0) {\n            Cluster cluster;\n            cluster.seed_point = best_seed;\n            cluster.members = best_cluster_members;\n            clusters.push_back(cluster);\n            \n            // Mark all members as clustered\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793070066966,"sessionID":"ses_e84b3166effePmOSLT1U4l8Om0","part":{"id":"prt_17b4d09900017NMyzixqLFpOq9","messageID":"msg_17b4d04200019OMCjS801vr1nT","sessionID":"ses_e84b3166effePmOSLT1U4l8Om0","type":"reasoning","text":"The output.txt file looks like a leftover log from a previous run, probably not critical, though I could skim it for hints about expected format or a baseline hash. I should focus instead on preserving key semantics like the sequential data generation using rand_r seeding.\n\nFor qtClustering, I'm tracing through the algorithm carefully: iterating unclustered seeds in ascending order, greedily growing candidate clusters, and picking the seed with strictly greater cardinality on ties. I'm noting the tie-breaking rules in findClosestPoint (strict less-than comparisons, ascending iteration order) and edge cases like when no closest point is found, since getting these details exactly right matters for matching the original behavior.\n\nThe complexity here is steep—for each unclustered seed, growing a cluster scans all N points against the current members, giving something like O(U * N * S²) per outer iteration, which makes this the dominant cost. I'm now thinking about how to parallelize the outer loop over seeds to cut this down.\n\nSince each seed's candidate cluster is independent given the current `clustered` state, I can distribute seeds across MPI ranks and have each rank find its own local best (max cardinality, smallest seed index as tiebreak). Then I'd reduce across ranks—using an allgather of (cardinality, seed) pairs so every rank deterministically computes the global winner—and broadcast that winner's member list to all ranks before proceeding to the next outer iteration.\n\nI distribute the shrinking unclustered list cyclically by index modulo rank count for reasonable balance, avoiding OpenMP since the scope calls for pure MPI. For the inner computation I want to preserve exact floating-point semantics, so I shouldn't swap sqrt-based distance comparisons for squared-distance comparisons since that could change rounding behavior at the margins.\n\nI realize I can incrementally track each candidate's max distance to the cluster as members are added, since max is order-independent and exact for non-NaN doubles — this cuts the per-step cost from O(N*S) to O(N), turning the overall complexity from O(N*S²) into O(N*S) per seed while producing bit-identical results. I'm now extending this incremental approach to the closest-point search, maintaining a running max-distance array across candidates as the cluster grows.\n\nOnce a candidate's tracked max distance exceeds the threshold, it can never qualify again since max only increases, so I can permanently prune it from the active candidate list for this growth pass — another exact optimization that avoids rescanning dead candidates while still breaking ties by lowest index.\n\nOverall per-seed growth costs roughly O(N·S), and across all unclustered seeds and outer iterations that becomes O(K·U·N·S) — still heavy for very large N, but a big improvement over the naive squared approach.\n\nI wonder whether seeds could be skipped if their cluster didn't change, but since removing points can alter greedy choices for future growths, that caching isn't exact. A better pruning idea: since every cluster member must be within distance < threshold of the seed itself, a seed's maximum possible cardinality is bounded by 1 plus however many unclustered points fall within that threshold distance — giving a cheap upper bound to prune seeds early.\n\nWithin a rank, since seeds are processed in ascending index order, I can compare this bound against the rank's running local-best cardinality: if the bound is less than or equal to the local best, this seed can't win (ties go to the earlier, smaller-index seed), so it's safe to skip without affecting the global result.\n\nVerifying the bound's validity: every member added to a cluster must be within threshold distance of the seed itself, so the max possible cluster size is one (the seed) plus the count of unclustered points within threshold of the seed — using the same distance function as the actual clustering scan, so this holds correctly. This bound check costs a linear scan over unclustered points per seed, which is cheap compared to full cluster growth.\n\nTo get the most benefit from pruning, I'm thinking of sorting seeds by their bound in descending order before evaluating them, with careful tie-breaking logic (comparing cluster size then seed index) so that pruning decisions stay exact rather than approximate. It adds some complexity but the potential speedup from early pruning seems worth it.\n\nI need to verify that pruned seeds truly can't beat the local best given the bound relations, and checking each case confirms the local best always dominates. Since the global winner is just the best among all local bests, and the ordering (card desc, seed asc) matches the original algorithm's tie-breaking by earliest seed index, the reduction should produce the same winner as the original sequential approach.\n\nNow I'm working out the communication step: ranks without any seeds send a sentinel value, and I need to confirm every rank that does have seeds always evaluates at least its first one since the initial best starts at zero cardinality. Then after an allgather determines the winning rank, that owner needs to broadcast its winning cluster's member list to all other ranks, which means every rank must preallocate a buffer sized to the winning cardinality before the broadcast call.\n\nI'm also thinking through cost: with K clusters this is only two small collectives per iteration, so overhead is minor, but seed assignment via cyclic distribution over unclustered positions could cause load imbalance since growth costs differ per seed — and computing bounds scans all unclustered points locally, so each iteration costs roughly N²/P work plus the growth evaluation cost for the chosen seed.\n\nI'm sketching the growth function itself: starting from a seed, maintaining an active candidate list with precomputed distances to the seed, pruning any candidate whose distance already exceeds threshold, then iteratively expanding membership from the remaining active set.\n\nI verify this matches the original algorithm: since active stays in ascending order without needing resorting, the first index achieving the minimum md value corresponds exactly to the original's tie-breaking behavior of picking the lowest-indexed candidate among ties, and the max-distance tracking logic lines up with how std::max is used in the original. I also need to double check that the original's exclusion logic for already-clustered points matches how I'm filtering the active set.\n\nI'm confirming the bound covers all members within threshold of the seed, computed by scanning unclustered indices for distance to seed. Then for the MPI outer loop, each rank computes bounds for its assigned local positions, sorts seeds by bound descending, and iterates with an early-break condition before evaluating actual growth.\n\nFor selecting the global winner, ranks exchange their best (card, seed) pairs via an allgather, pick the max by cardinality then smallest seed (idle ranks default to card 0), broadcast the winning cluster's members from that rank, and append the new cluster to a list kept identical across all ranks before marking those points clustered and removing them from the unclustered set.\n\nFor timing and output, I measure clustering duration with barriers and MPI_Wtime, reducing with MPI_MAX across ranks to get the worst-case elapsed time while keeping the print format unchanged, and only rank 0 handles printing and validation since all ranks hold the same cluster data; I need to make sure every rank returns a consistent exit code before MPI_Finalize.\n\nI confirm the distance arithmetic stays byte-identical across the bound check, growth, and validation since they all reuse the same inline distance function, so FMA contraction can't introduce divergence between ranks. The CMake setup needs find_package(MPI REQUIRED) with the imported MPI::MPI_CXX target, keeping the same executable name and optimization flags.\n\nBefore touching anything, I want to build the original single-process version as a baseline so I can diff its output against my MPI version for correctness, so I'm saving a copy and checking whether mpicxx is available to compile it.\n\n","time":{"start":1793070008720,"end":1793070066911},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793070412167,"sessionID":"ses_e84b3166effePmOSLT1U4l8Om0","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_019BdiqEXEGAywyLGBxxR8hf","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/qtclustering_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r4/qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp","content":"// QT Clustering Benchmark - MPI Distributed Version\n//\n// QT (Quality Threshold) clustering is an algorithm that builds clusters\n// by starting with a seed point and iteratively adding the closest point\n// that maintains the cluster's diameter below a threshold.\n//\n// Parallelization: in every round of the main loop, the candidate seeds are\n// distributed cyclically across MPI ranks. Each rank grows candidate clusters\n// from its local seeds and the globally best candidate (largest cardinality,\n// lowest seed index on ties, matching the sequential first-wins rule) is\n// selected with an allgather. The owning rank broadcasts the winning members.\n// Every rank then applies the identical state update, so the clustering result\n// is identical to the sequential algorithm for any number of processes.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <numeric>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Scratch buffers reused across candidate growths to avoid reallocation\nstruct GrowScratch {\n    std::vector<int> active;     // unclustered candidates still admissible, ascending index\n    std::vector<double> maxd;    // running max distance from each active candidate to the cluster\n};\n\n// Greedily grow a candidate cluster from `seed`.\n//\n// Semantically identical to repeatedly calling \"find the unclustered, not yet\n// in-cluster point whose max distance to the cluster is smallest and < threshold\n// (lowest index on ties)\" and adding it. The max distance of each candidate is\n// tracked incrementally instead of being recomputed against all members. Because\n// max is exact and order-independent, the values are bit-identical to the\n// recomputed ones. A candidate whose max distance reaches the threshold can never\n// be admitted again, so it is dropped permanently.\nvoid growCluster(const int seed,\n                 const std::vector<char>& clustered,\n                 const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                 const double threshold,\n                 GrowScratch& scratch,\n                 std::vector<int>& members) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    std::vector<int>& active = scratch.active;\n    std::vector<double>& maxd = scratch.maxd;\n\n    members.clear();\n    members.push_back(seed);\n\n    active.clear();\n    maxd.clear();\n    const Point& seed_pt = points[seed];\n    for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c) {\n        if (c == seed || clustered[c]) continue;\n        const double d = distance(points[c], seed_pt);\n        if (d < threshold) {\n            active.push_back(c);\n            maxd.push_back(d);\n        }\n    }\n    if (active.empty()) return;\n\n    // Position of the admissible candidate with the smallest max distance\n    // (first occurrence on ties, i.e. lowest index since active is ascending)\n    size_t best = 0;\n    for (size_t k = 1; k < active.size(); ++k) {\n        if (maxd[k] < maxd[best]) best = k;\n    }\n\n    while (true) {\n        const int chosen = active[best];\n        members.push_back(chosen);\n        const Point& chosen_pt = points[chosen];\n\n        // Update max distances against the new member and compact survivors\n        // (order preserved), tracking the next best candidate in the same pass.\n        size_t w = 0;\n        size_t next_best = static_cast<size_t>(-1);\n        double next_val = 0.0;\n        const size_t n = active.size();\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n            if (k == best) continue;\n            const double m = std::max(maxd[k], distance(points[active[k]], chosen_pt));\n            if (m < threshold) {\n                active[w] = active[k];\n                maxd[w] = m;\n                if (next_best == static_cast<size_t>(-1) || m < next_val) {\n                    next_best = w;\n                    next_val = m;\n                }\n                ++w;\n            }\n        }\n        active.resize(w);\n        maxd.resize(w);\n\n        if (next_best == static_cast<size_t>(-1)) break;\n        best = next_best;\n    }\n}\n\n// Upper bound on the cardinality of any cluster grown from `seed`: every member\n// other than the seed must be an unclustered point within the threshold of the seed\n// (the candidate's max distance includes the seed itself).\nint cardinalityBound(const int seed,\n                     const std::vector<int>& unclustered,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold) {\n    int bound = 1;\n    const Point& seed_pt = points[seed];\n    for (const int u : unclustered) {\n        if (u != seed && distance(points[u], seed_pt) < threshold) {\n            ++bound;\n        }\n    }\n    return bound;\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm (MPI-parallel over candidate seeds)\nstd::vector<Cluster> qtClustering(const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                  const double threshold,\n                                  const int rank,\n                                  const int nprocs) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    std::vector<char> clustered(N, 0);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered(N);  // always ascending\n    std::iota(unclustered.begin(), unclustered.end(), 0);\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n\n    GrowScratch scratch;\n    std::vector<int> candidate_members;\n    std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> order;  // (bound, seed)\n\n    while (!unclustered.empty()) {\n        // Local seeds: positions p in the unclustered list with p % nprocs == rank\n        order.clear();\n        const size_t U = unclustered.size();\n        for (size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(rank); p < U; p += static_cast<size_t>(nprocs)) {\n            const int seed = unclustered[p];\n            order.emplace_back(cardinalityBound(seed, unclustered, points, threshold), seed);\n        }\n        // Evaluate most promising seeds first; ties by ascending seed index\n        std::sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [](const auto& a, const auto& b) {\n            if (a.first != b.first) return a.first > b.first;\n            return a.second < b.second;\n        });\n\n        // Local best under (cardinality desc, seed asc)\n        int best_card = 0;\n        int best_seed = INT_MAX;\n        std::vector<int> best_members;\n        for (const auto& [bound, seed] : order) {\n            // Remaining seeds cannot beat the local best (sorted by bound, then seed)\n            if (bound < best_card || (bound == best_card && seed > best_seed)) break;\n\n            growCluster(seed, clustered, points, threshold, scratch, candidate_members);\n            const int card = static_cast<int>(candidate_members.size());\n            if (card > best_card || (card == best_card && seed < best_seed)) {\n                best_card = card;\n                best_seed = seed;\n                best_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Global best across ranks with the same ordering\n        const int local[2] = {best_card, best_seed};\n        std::vector<int> all(2 * static_cast<size_t>(nprocs));\n        MPI_Allgather(local, 2, MPI_INT, all.data(), 2, MPI_INT, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        int win_card = 0;\n        int win_seed = INT_MAX;\n        int win_rank = -1;\n        for (int r = 0; r < nprocs; ++r) {\n            const int c = all[2 * r];\n            const int s = all[2 * r + 1];\n            if (c > 0 && (c > win_card || (c == win_card && s < win_seed))) {\n                win_card = c;\n                win_seed = s;\n                win_rank = r;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No cluster can be formed (cannot happen while unclustered points exist)\n        if (win_rank < 0 || win_card <= 0) break;\n\n        // Share the winning cluster's members with all ranks\n        std::vector<int> members;\n        if (rank == win_rank) {\n            members = best_members;\n        } else {\n            members.resize(win_card);\n        }\n        MPI_Bcast(members.data(), win_card, MPI_INT, win_rank, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        Cluster cluster;\n        cluster.seed_point = win_seed;\n        cluster.members = std::move(members);\n        for (const int m : cluster.members) {\n            clustered[m] = 1;\n        }\n        clusters.push_back(std::move(cluster));\n\n        // Remove clustered points from unclustered list (order preserved)\n        unclustered.erase(\n            std::remove_if(unclustered.begin(), unclustered.end(),\n                           [&clustered](int idx) { return clustered[idx] != 0; }),\n            unclustered.end());\n    }\n\n    return clusters;\n}\n\n// Validation: check that clusters satisfy the QT clustering properties\nbool validateClusters(const std::vector<Cluster>& clusters,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold) {\n    bool valid = true;\n    \n    printf(\"Validating clusters:\\n\");\n    \n    // Check each cluster\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        const auto& cluster = clusters[c];\n        double max_diameter = 0.0;\n        \n        // Check diameter (max distance between any two points)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster.members.size(); ++i) {\n            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < cluster.members.size(); ++j) {\n                const double dist = distance(points[cluster.members[i]], \n                                           points[cluster.members[j]]);\n                max_diameter = std::max(max_diameter, dist);\n            }\n        }\n        \n        if (c < 10) { // Print first 10 clusters\n            printf(\"  Cluster %zu: size=%zu, seed=%d, diameter=%.4f\\n\", \n                   c, cluster.members.size(), cluster.seed_point, max_diameter);\n        }\n        \n        // Validate diameter is within threshold\n        if (max_diameter > threshold * 1.001) { // Allow small numerical error\n            printf(\"ERROR: Cluster %zu has diameter %.4f > threshold %.4f\\n\", \n                   c, max_diameter, threshold);\n            valid = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check for duplicate memberships\n    std::vector<int> membership(points.size(), -1);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = clusters[c].members[i];\n            if (membership[member] >= 0) {\n                printf(\"ERROR: Point %d appears in multiple clusters (%d and %zu)\\n\",\n                       member, membership[member], c);\n                valid = false;\n            }\n            membership[member] = static_cast<int>(c);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Count clustered points\n    int clustered_count = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < membership.size(); ++i) {\n        if (membership[i] >= 0) clustered_count++;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Total points: %zu, Clustered: %d, Unclustered: %zu\\n\",\n           points.size(), clustered_count, points.size() - clustered_count);\n    \n    return valid;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of points (default: 1000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -t <float>   Distance threshold for clustering (default: 2.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int nprocs = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &nprocs);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    int num_points = 1000;\n    double threshold = 2.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            num_points = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-t\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            threshold = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (num_points <= 0 || threshold <= 0.0) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Error: Invalid parameters (num_points=%d, threshold=%.2f)\\n\", \n                   num_points, threshold);\n        }\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"QT Clustering Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of points: %d\\n\", num_points);\n        printf(\"Distance threshold: %.2f\\n\", threshold);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n    \n    // Generate synthetic data (deterministic, replicated on every rank)\n    std::vector<Point> points(num_points);\n    generateSyntheticData(points, num_points);\n    \n    // Perform QT clustering\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const double t_start = MPI_Wtime();\n    \n    const std::vector<Cluster> clusters = qtClustering(points, threshold, rank, nprocs);\n    \n    const double t_local = MPI_Wtime() - t_start;\n    double t_max = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&t_local, &t_max, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const long cluster_ms = static_cast<long>(t_max * 1000.0);\n    \n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Clustering time: %ld ms\\n\", cluster_ms);\n        printf(\"Clusters found: %zu\\n\", clusters.size());\n    }\n    \n    // Calculate statistics and performance metrics\n    int total_clustered = 0;\n    int max_cluster_size = 0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters.size(); ++i) {\n        const int size = static_cast<int>(clusters[i].members.size());\n        total_clustered += size;\n        max_cluster_size = std::max(max_cluster_size, size);\n    }\n    \n    const double avg_cluster_size = clusters.empty() ? 0.0 : \n        static_cast<double>(total_clustered) / clusters.size();\n    \n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Points clustered: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\\n\", \n               total_clustered, num_points, \n               100.0 * total_clustered / num_points);\n        printf(\"Average cluster size: %.2f\\n\", avg_cluster_size);\n        printf(\"Maximum cluster size: %d\\n\", max_cluster_size);\n        \n        // Performance metrics\n        const double time_sec = cluster_ms / 1000.0;\n        const double clusters_per_sec = clusters.size() / time_sec;\n        const double points_per_sec = num_points / time_sec;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.1f clusters/s, %.1f points/s\\n\", \n               clusters_per_sec, points_per_sec);\n    }\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults && root) {\n        // Serialize cluster membership for hashing\n        std::vector<double> membershipData;\n        membershipData.reserve(num_points);\n        std::vector<int> membership(num_points, -1);\n        for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n                membership[clusters[c].members[i]] = static_cast<int>(c);\n            }\n        }\n        for (int m : membership) {\n            membershipData.push_back(static_cast<double>(m));\n        }\n        print_results(membershipData, \"ClusterMembership\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation (performed on root; status broadcast so all ranks agree on exit code)\n    int status = 0;\n    if (validate) {\n        int valid = 1;\n        if (root) {\n            valid = FAILED\\n\");\n            }\n        }\n        MPI_Bcast(&valid, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        status = valid ? 0 : 1;\n    }\n    \n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return
